# Physical parser origins v1 — proposed freeze contract

Design/test draft only; no producer implementation or submission. Source observation PR5055 remains separate. Missing command on baseline is FEATURE ABSENCE, never compiler semantic red.

Command: `rz source-origins <file> --source-key <key> --profile physical-origins-v1`. Both options required exactly once. No typecheck, solver, execution, import resolution or mutable package lookup. Key is caller-supplied logical identity, explicitly NOT an authenticated path; physical input filename is I/O only and is not substituted for key. Local literal `use` can be parsed but never followed. This reports exactly one physical buffer.

Key grammar: UTF-8 string limited to1024bytes; canonical slash-separated ASCII components [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+, no empty component, absolute root, '.', '..', backslash, colon or NUL; final filename ends `.rz`. Unknown profile/missing/duplicate option or invalid key is CLI rejection. Requested metadata limits only:1MiB buffer,65536tokens,128lexical scope/delimiter depth,4096declarations,8192clauses. Stable-filesystem profile: reject final-component symlinks and nonregular paths using symlink_metadata before File::open, recheck opened handle metadata is regular, then bounded read. Static FIFO/directory/symlink rejection is tested before open. Concurrent path replacement/TOCTOU and inherited file-descriptor/process-group adversaries are EXCLUDED; no O_NONBLOCK/no-follow/race-safe guarantee is claimed. Intermediate directory symlinks are outside containment/authentication claims. No new unsafe/dependencies or normal parse-path changes. Existing source readers are NOT nonblocking templates; input errors/limits yield no partial accepted origins. Limits never change normal parse wrappers/language acceptance. Accepted stdout (including final newline) is capped at524288bytes, below the harness1MiB capture cap. If serialization would exceed this limit, emit a small whole-unit resource-limit rejection, never partial JSON/IDs.

Initial declaration grammar follows independently reviewed inventory: ASCII identifiers, UTF-8 comments/string bodies, function/module/simple struct/impl plus literal local .rz use with optional alias; primitive/named nongeneric types and bounded parameters (self only methods); requires/ensures scalar contracts; balanced bodies with no declaration-bearing fn/mod/impl/use/requires/ensures tokens. No pub/attributes/effect annotations/generics/traits/macros/builtins/package/selectors/globs/field-or-call contract expressions. Encountering unsupported grammar OR any real parser/recovery error rejects the whole unit, never partial accepted arrays/IDs. Accepted syntax is provenance only, not frontend validity/proof eligibility. Real Parser callbacks and token extents supply origins; no second inventory lexer, normalized-text search or bare-name reverse matching.

Accepted stdout: single JSON object schema `resilient-physical-origins/v1`, profile, source_key, key_authority=`caller-supplied-not-authenticated-path`, file_sha256, bytes, disposition=`accepted`, declarations[], sites[]. Arrays in physical source order. Zero-clause functions/methods appear in declarations with empty site_ids. Simple structs/use are supported structural syntax but not function declaration records. Every site references exactly one declaration_id; arrays have unique IDs, no silent dedup. Exit0 only accepted. Rejection: mandatory schema/profile/source_key/key_authority/file_sha256/bytes envelope fields (profile and key echo requested values or null when missing; file_sha256/bytes null until safely available), disposition=`rejected`, error {code,message}; NO declarations/sites/declaration_id/site_id/identity/origins keys at ANY recursive depth. This applies even inside errors/diagnostics, not merely top-level arrays. Caller-controlled key/profile echoes are inert data, including strings beginning decl-sha256: or site-sha256:; string spelling alone NEVER establishes an accepted typed-origin ID. Negative tests require invalid key decl-sha256:x.rz and unsupported profile site-sha256:x to echo unchanged without accepted-origin containers. Exit1 parse/unsupported/resource; exit2 CLI/key/profile/input. Error code categories are frozen separately (not exact prose).

Canonical identity JSON: compact UTF-8, lexicographically sorted object keys recursively, no whitespace, no Unicode escaping except JSON-required control escapes, lowercase SHA256hex, integers decimal, arrays preserve order; hash exactly encoded identity object bytes. No display/output-envelope fields enter IDs. IDs prefix `decl-sha256:` or `site-sha256:` plus digest. Required profile is externally selected, never inferred from output.

Declaration identity keys: schema=`resilient-physical-declaration/v1`, profile, source_key, file_sha256, kind (`function` or `method`), scope (ordered typed components {kind:`module`|`impl`,name:originalidentifier}; traitunsupported), name (original unmangled), fn_keyword_byte, declaration_byte_range, declaration_sha256, header_byte_range, header_sha256. Ranges half-open UTF8bytes. Declaration begins fn keyword (modifier syntax unsupported) and ends just after matching body `}`. Header starts same fn and ends just before body `{` (includes intervening whitespace). Char offsets must be converted with an exact-buffer boundary table. Source order distinguishes repeated declarations; duplicate semantic names can still be physically inventoried without claiming frontend validity.

Site identity keys: schema=`resilient-physical-clause/v1`, profile, source_key, file_sha256, declaration_id, clause_kind (`requires`|`ensures`), ordinal (per-kind source order), full_clause_byte_range, full_clause_sha256, expression_byte_range, expression_sha256. Full clause starts keyword and ends after expression's last token; excludes trailing trivia before next clause/body. Expression starts first expression token after keyword, ends same last-token boundary. Internal comments/whitespace remain exact slice bytes. Site records include identity object+site_id, declaration records identity+declaration_id+site_ids. No declaration/site IDs for synthetic parser fallbacks.

Tests must freeze manual source/ranges/canonical JSON before code. Compare exact identity data and IDs, zero-clause inventory and lexical scopes. Reject invalid/recovery/unsupported wholeunits, wrong CLI key/profile, resource excess. Keep baseline missingcommand records as featureabsence and per-case actual reachability honest. Parser-origin claims remain separate from imported binding instances, proof export and feasibility/path correspondence. No existing schema/help/golden/test edits or CI changes implied.


Revision2 deterministic precedence: validate command/options/key/profile first; reject input symlink/nonregular/open/size before UTF8 decoding under the stated stable-filesystem assumption. Buffer limit error.limit=source-bytes. Invalid UTF8 rejects exit2/code invalid-utf8 with no origins. Run a bounded preflight of the SAME real Lexer token stream before parser callbacks: exclude EOF from token budget; check each token in deterministic order token-count then delimiter-depth then Function keyword count then Requires/Ensures keyword count. String/comment contents are not keyword tokens. Counters are candidate token kinds, not accepted declaration/site counts. Limits error.limit respectively tokens, delimiter-depth, function-keywords, contract-keywords. This phase makes limit fixtures reach their target before grammar/parse-error precedence. No independent lexer or text scanner is added. Tokenize once/cache or share exact token stream; preserve normal parser wrappers. Lexical invalidity without resource excess rejects parse-error; actual parse/recovery failure OR any contract parse_expression returning None latches whole-unit provenance rejection even when existing fallback creates synthetic true without parser.errors. Accepted-origin callbacks cannot commit partial arrays. Only after successful parser+profile checks evaluate serialized output budget (error.limit=output-bytes); all lower-level limit cases therefore precede output size.

Original five vectors/IDs remain byte-identical historical requirements; new vectors add literal-use alias with nonexistent target (proves no resolver should run), nested typed module/impl scopes, separate interleaved repeated-requires/ensures, and the independently reviewed77byte parentheses/comment oracle. Oracle offsets: fn6, declaration[6,76), header[6,63), fullclause[25,55), expression[33,55); trailing UTF8comment[55,63) excluded from expression/clause but retained in header. This captures physical parentheses/internal comments lost by AST-only spans. Recovery requires{ and ensures{ are separate whole-unit rejection fixtures. Baseline absence is still unexecuted until hosted observation and never a semantic compiler red.

Duplicate option envelope rule: a duplicated key/profile field echoes null because ambiguous; uniquely supplied other field remains echoed. Missing fields echo null. Unknown/trailing arguments retain uniquely supplied key/profile echoes. File hash/bytes are mandatory null until safely available.
